'''''The Sneetches and Other Stories''''' is a collection of stories by American children's author [[Dr. Seuss]], published in 1961.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Geisel |first=Theodor |title=The Sneetches and Other Stories |publisher=Random House |year=1961 <!-- ISBN omitted as this is a pre-1965 work --> |location=New York}}</ref> It is composed of four separate stories with themes of tolerance, diversity, and compromise: "The Sneetches", "The Zax", "Too Many Daves", and "What Was I Scared Of?" Based on an online poll, the [[National Education Association]] listed the book as one of its "Teachers' Top 100 Books for Children".<ref name="NEA2007">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nea.org/grants/13154.htm |title=Teachers' Top 100 Books for Children |date=2007 |publisher=National Education Association |access-date=2012-08-22}}</ref> In 2012 it was ranked number 63 among the Top 100 Picture Books in a survey published by ''[[School Library Journal]]'' – the fifth of five Dr. Seuss books on the list.<ref name="SLJPicture2012">{{Cite web |url=http://blog.schoollibraryjournal.com/afuse8production/2012/07/06/top-100-picture-books-poll-results |title=Top 100 Picture Books Poll Results |last=Bird, Elizabeth |date=July 6, 2012 |publisher=A Fuse #8 Production. Blog. [[School Library Journal]] (blog.schoollibraryjournal.com) |access-date=2012-08-22 |archive-date=2012-12-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121204030956/http://blog.schoollibraryjournal.com/afuse8production/2012/07/06/top-100-picture-books-poll-results |url-status=dead}}</ref>

"The Sneetches" and "The Zax" were later adapted, along with ''[[Green Eggs and Ham]]'', into 1973's animated TV musical special ''[[Dr. Seuss on the Loose]]: The Sneetches, The Zax, Green Eggs and Ham'' with [[Hans Conried]] voicing the narrator and both Zax, [[Paul Winchell]] voicing the Sneetches, and [[Bob Holt (actor)|Bob Holt]] voicing Sylvester McMonkey McBean.

In 2022, it was announced that a 45-minute CGI animated special based on ''The Sneetches'' was in development for [[Netflix]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Petski |first1=Denise |title=Netflix Orders Five Dr. Seuss-Inspired Animated Preschool Series & Specials |url=https://deadline.com/2022/03/netflix-orders-five-dr-seuss-inspired-animated-preschool-series-specials-1234978854/ |website=Deadline |access-date=March 15, 2022 |date=March 15, 2022}}</ref> In 2025, it was announced the special was now turned into a television series that will be released in fall 2025.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lang|first=Jamie|title='Minecraft,' 'Clash of Clans,' 'Magic the Gathering' and 'Ghostbusters' Series Teased at Netflix Annecy Studio Focus|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/global/minecraft-clash-of-clans-magic-the-gathering-netflix-1236429388/|website=Variety|date=June 11, 2025|access-date=June 11, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Milligan|first=Mercedes|url=https://www.animationmagazine.net/2025/06/netflix-lines-up-a-fully-animated-slate-thru-2025/|title=Netflix Lines Up a Lively Animated Feature and Series Slate Thru 2025|website=[[Animation Magazine]]|date=June 18, 2025|access-date=June 18, 2025}}</ref>

==Stories==
===The Sneetches===
[[File:SneetchesRedbook1953.webp|thumb|270px|The 1953 ''[[Redbook]]'' version of "The Sneetches"]] 
The first story in the collection tells of a group of yellow bird-like creatures, the Sneetches, some of whom have a green star on their bellies. At the beginning of the story, Sneetches with stars [[discriminate]] against and shun those without. An entrepreneur/[[Scam|con-artist]] named Sylvester McMonkey McBean (calling himself "the Fix-It-Up Chappie") appears and offers the Sneetches without stars the chance to get them with his Star-On machine, for three dollars. The treatment is instantly popular, but this upsets the original Star-Bellied Sneetches, as they are in danger of losing their special status. McBean then tells them about his Star-Off machine, costing ten dollars, and the Sneetches who originally had stars happily pay the money to have them removed in order to remain special. However, McBean does not share the prejudices of the Sneetches and allows the recently starred Sneetches through this machine as well. Ultimately, this escalates, with the Sneetches running from one machine to the next,

: "Until neither the Plain nor the Star-Bellies knew
: Whether this one was that one... or that one was this one
: Or which one was what one... or what one was who."

This continues until the Sneetches are [[penniless]] and McBean departs as a rich man, amused by their folly. Despite his assertion that "you can't teach a Sneetch", the Sneetches learn from this experience that neither Plain-Bellied nor Star-Bellied Sneetches are superior, and they are able to get along and become friends.
{{external media| float = left| video1 = [https://www.c-span.org/video/?311256-2/civil-human-rights-themes-dr-seuss-the-sneetches-yertle-turtle Panel discussion on "Civil and Human Rights Themes in Dr. Seuss' ''The Sneetches'' and ''Yertle the Turtle''", New York Law School, March 1, 2013], [[C-SPAN]]}}

"The Sneetches" was intended by Seuss as a satire of discrimination between races and cultures, and was specifically inspired by his [[Anti-antisemitism|opposition to antisemitism]].<ref name="Scott">{{Cite book |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/pipersatgatesofd00cott |title=Pipers at the Gates of Dawn: The Wisdom of Children's Literature |last=Jonathan Cott |publisher=[[Random House]] |year=1983 |isbn=978-0-394-50464-3 |location=[[New York, New York|New York]] |chapter=The Good Dr. Seuss |oclc=8728388 |quote=...children's literature as I write it and as I see it is satire to a great extent ... there's ''The Sneetches'' ... which was inspired by my opposition to anti-Semitism |chapter-format=Reprint |chapter-url-access=registration}}</ref>

The Sneetches first appeared in a short poem, also called "The Sneetches", but including neither McBean nor his machine, that was published in ''[[Redbook]]'' magazine in 1953. 

===The Zax===
[[File:ZaksRedbook1954.webp|thumb|270px|The 1954 ''Redbook'' version, "The Zaks"]]
In "The Zax", a North-going Zax and a South-going Zax meet face to face on the Prairie of Prax. Each asks the other to make way, but neither budges, saying it is against their upbringing to move any other way. Because they stubbornly refuse to move (east, west, or any direction except their respective headings) to get past each other, the two Zaxes then face off against each other with their arms crossed. The Zaxes stand so long that eventually a [[highway overpass]] is built around them. The story ends with the Zaxes still standing there "unbudged" in their tracks.

A different version of the story, "The Zaks", with a more absolute outcome for its differently-named characters, was printed in ''[[Redbook]]'' magazine in 1954.

===Too Many Daves===
"Too Many Daves" is a very short story about a mother, Mrs. McCave, who named all 23 of her sons Dave. This causes minor problems in the family when she calls one of them, but instead, they all come, and the rest of the story lists unusual and amusing names she wishes she had given them, such as "Bodkin Van Horn", "Hoos Foos", "Snimm", "Hot-Shot", "Shadrack", "Stuffy", "Stinky", "Putt-Putt", "Buffalo Bill", "Oliver Boliver Butt", "Biffalo Buff" or "Zanzibar Buck-Buck McFate". The story ends with the statement that "she didn't do it, and now it's too late."

===What Was I Scared Of?===
"What Was I Scared Of?" tells the tale of a character who frequently encounters an empty pair of pale-green [[Trousers|pants]] in dark and spooky locations. The character, who is the narrator, is initially afraid of the pants, which are able to stand freely despite the lack of a wearer. However, when he screams for help, the pants also start to cry, and he realizes that "they were just as scared as I!" The empty pants and the narrator become friends. This is one of the few Seuss works in verse that is not [[Anapestic tetrameter]].

== Distribution by NATO in Bosnia ==
{{update section|date=September 2018}}
In 1998, [[NATO]] translated the collection into [[Serbo-Croatian]] and planned to distribute 500,000 copies to children in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], as part of a campaign to encourage tolerance.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_1998_August_10/ai_50233312 |title=Agency of NATO and United Nations to Distribute Dr. Seuss Stories to Foster Racial Tolerance in War-Torn Bosnia |date=August 10, 1998 |work=Business Wire |access-date=2006-10-16 |publisher=Business Wire, Inc. |quote=Random House Children's Publishing and Dr. Seuss Enterprises announced today that ''The Sneetches and Other Stories'', a book by the celebrated children's author Dr. Seuss, will be translated by NATO into Serbo-Croatian and distributed in the fall to 500,000 children in Bosnia and Herzegovina as part of an information campaign to help encourage racial tolerance.}}</ref> This was later scaled back to 50,000 copies at a cost of $120,000 as well as looking for a more appropriate source of funding such as an [[Non-governmental organization|NGO]], private charity or corporation, as this expenditure did not meet the "Minimum Military Requirement" test for NATO common funding eligibility.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/WPcap/2000-02/09/032r-020900-idx.html |title=NATO Going for Green Eggs on Its Face |date=2000-02-09 |newspaper=Washington Post |access-date=2019-08-08}}</ref>
